dream: I pressed the flat top down hard until the slip felt real. The wedge felt thin under the axe, sliding into the air that smelled of wet paper. I swapped a tall rock for a small one to stop the lazy slide, but the roof stayed high, heavy as a breath I cannot catch. The turnip squished in the stack, damp and real, while the hot card hummed, making the thin edge feel suddenly heavy. I slept through the weight, trusting the lean.
